messages:
Sara: Heads-up — noticed a persistent 95p latency bump on dashboards starting ~09:00 UTC. Traces point to a "slow path" in the query layer that kicks in for some tenant queries (large filters + cross-join aggregations).
Sara: It's not a single hot tenant, more like ~2% of requests that go into a heavy plan and then fan out. UI blocks while waiting; user impact visible.
Devin: Do we have the sample traces? can we repro in staging with a similar dataset?
Sara: Pasted a couple of short traces: `query-id: 0xabc123` — backend spends ~600ms on authz + 1.4s on plan execution.
Sara: Hypothesis: authz lookups for deep-perm sets + large tile enumeration triggers a slow planner path. Also cache miss on tenant-prefetch.
Julia: Are those authz calls hitting external IAM every time? we added a per-request token exchange last quarter that might be resurfacing.
Samir: From runtime POV the slow path is where we expand projections into N tenant tiles and then do per-tenant permission checks inline. That explosion is the root cause.
Kevin: TL;DR: two knobs we can try: 1) avoid expanding before authz by short-circuiting via an authz-only preflight, 2) add a cost-estimation hint so the console can choose a cheaper projection.
Devin: I like the cost hint idea for progressive degradation. We could add a small contract so query-service returns `estimated_units` and `is_heavy` in the planning phase. Frontend can then render a low-fidelity view or request `prefer_fast=true`.
Samir: Proposed API tweak (very small):
```
// request header
Prefer-Fast: true|false
// planning response
X-Estimated-Units: "42"
X-Is-Heavy: "true"
```
Samir: If `Prefer-Fast` is set, query planner can favor a fast-but-approximate projection or return a `304 PARTIAL_VIEW` with a pointer to a snapshot.
Julia: Be careful: RBAC semantics must not change. Any fast path must be permission-preserving. We can only return approximate data if we also flag it and show stale/partial badge in the UI.
Sara: Agree. UX must show partial/stale. For many dashboards a partial tile is better than blocking the whole page.
Kevin: Tradeoffs: exposing `X-Estimated-Units` leaks cost model surface to clients. Could be okay internally but don't want it relied on by third-party integrations.
Devin: Keep it internal for now, flag protected header `X-Infra-Estimate` and mark in docs as unstable.
Samir: Another optimization: move per-tenant authz checks to a batched evaluation step using tenant-chunks + cached claim sets to avoid N calls. That reduces authz overhead and prevents plan explosion.
Julia: That would need an auth cache invalidation strategy. Regulated tenants won't like stale perms. Suggest TTL + revocation webhook.
Sara: Operational mitigation first: deploy a temporary rate-limiter on the query path that detects >500ms authz+plan time and forces `Prefer-Fast` semantics. This would act as an emergency throttle.
Kevin: Sounds reasonable for quick mitigation. But long-term: change the interface and add the estimator + batched authz.
Devin: I'll add a light-weight 1% synthetic probe FIFO to run heavy queries in staging and compare planner behavior so we can get deterministic repro.
ops-bot: deploy:ci created job `canary/slow-path-mitigation` — runs smoke + perf checks on canary cluster.
Sara: Ownership: I'll open a short RFC for the `Prefer-Fast` header + planner signals. Samir — can you pair on the batched-authz sketch?
Samir: Yep, I'll sketch a design doc and a small proto this week.
Julia: I'll draft the auth cache invalidation section (TTL, webhook contract, audit log).
Kevin: I'll scope the rollout plan: feature flag, canary % (start 1% -> 10% -> 50%), SLO guardrails (error rate and 95p latency), and a rollback path.
Devin: Metric changes: add `query.planner.estimated_units`, `query.slow_path.triggered`, `query.prefer_fast_used` to telemetry. Also a small dashboard to track which tenants get downgraded so we can contact customers.
Sara: Final ask: let's avoid touching public API surfaces for now. Keep headers/internal flags behind feature flags and internal doc. We want to be able to iterate without long deprecation cycles.
Kevin: Agreed. Plan: mitigations PR -> canary -> small RFC for contract -> full implementation with batched authz & estimator.
Sara: Great. I'll drop RFC link here once created. Thanks everyone. :+1:
Devin: Thanks — will add synthetic job and a staging repro harness.
ops-bot: reminder: oncall rotation change next week — @eng-oncall please note the canary run windows.
